title: Saturn's Secret Shape: A Giant 10-Sided Storm!
summary:
Have you ever seen a storm that's a perfect shape? Well, Saturn has one! NASA's Hubble Space Telescope just found a huge, 10-sided wave circling Saturn's south pole. That's like a stop sign, but with two more sides! It's the first time we've seen such a big, regular pattern in Saturn's southern half.

Saturn already has a famous hexagon (a six-sided shape) at its north pole. That one has been there for over 40 years! But this new decagon (that's a 10-sided shape) is different. It looks like it's still growing, and scientists are excited to watch it develop.

How did they find it? Well, Saturn has seasons, just like Earth. As its seasons changed, the south pole became visible from Earth again. Amateur astronomers (people who love space and use their own telescopes) first noticed a faint wavy band in 2024. Then, in 2025, they saw it was a decagon! Scientists used Hubble to get a closer look.

One scientist, Agustín Sánchez-Lavega, said they've been looking for a southern hexagon since 1990, but never found one. Now, this new decagon appears! It's inside one of Saturn's powerful jet streams (fast winds). And it's not just on top of the clouds—it goes deep into the atmosphere.

The most amazing part? No one knows why it formed now. "The question is, why did it suddenly form now when we haven't seen one before?" said another scientist. Scientists will keep watching with Hubble and the James Webb Space Telescope to learn more. This shows how Hubble's long life helps us see changes on planets over many years. What will Saturn do next? Stay tuned!
why_it_matters: It shows why it is worth being curious about space—you never know when a telescope might uncover a surprise like a storm shaped like a stop sign with two extra sides.

background_read: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and is famous for its rings.
Saturn has seasons just like Earth, so different parts of the planet can become easier or harder to see as it orbits the Sun.
NASA's Hubble Space Telescope (a large telescope that circles Earth) has been watching the planets for decades.
Article_Structure: WHO: NASA scientists using the Hubble Space Telescope, helped by amateur astronomers with their own telescopes.
WHAT: They spotted a giant 10-sided wave, called a decagon, circling Saturn's south pole.
WHERE: On Saturn, near its south pole and deep in its atmosphere.
WHY: Saturn's changing seasons made the south pole visible again, and scientists do not yet know why this decagon suddenly appeared.

perspectives.description: They are excited because this is the first such pattern seen in Saturn's southern half, and they want to learn how it grows.
They helped spot the storm with their own telescopes, which shows that anyone can make a real discovery.
They admit they do not know why the decagon formed now, so they will keep watching to solve the mystery.
